briefing.headline: Three fresh, sponsorship-safe PMM reqs landed in the last 48 hours — hit those before the Boston repeats.
briefing.focus: Spend the first 12 minutes on Stripe's GTM PMM (Commerce) and Figma's Audience & Messaging PMM — both posted Aug 11, both large-cap H-1B sponsors, and Stripe is a direct banking/fintech domain carryover. Then take the Anthropic Product Marketing Ops req that posted today before the volume hits. Only after that, re-touch the Boston standbys (AWS Storage PMM, CarGurus) with a rewritten opener — they've been surfaced repeatedly and a fifth identical application won't change the outcome.

ranked.why: Posted yesterday, US-wide, Stripe = top-tier sponsor, and commerce/payments GTM is a straight lift from 6 years in banking/fintech.
Audience & Messaging PMM is literally segmentation + positioning — her two strongest skills — at a public company that sponsors, posted Aug 11.
Posted today; PMM Ops blends her Eloqua/HubSpot/SFDC ops chops with PMM craft, and the 78 keyword score badly under-reads it.
The only true Boston PMM req from a guaranteed sponsor — still worth a fifth swing, but only with a rewritten storage-specific opener.
Braze is martech: her Eloqua/HubSpot/GA4 stack is the product, and partner PMM rewards sales-collateral and competitive-intel work.
Fresh Aug 11 Amazon BA req, never pushed before — clean analyst-lane entry at a company that files H-1Bs at scale.
6sense IS the ABM category — her ABM experience is the whole job spec, and remote-US removes the relocation problem; the 58 ATS score is noise.
Datadog PMM at the right level, strong sponsor, and infra/AI positioning pairs with the STEM MBA in ML.
Demand-gen measurement for AWS Marketing is the exact intersection of both lanes — still a bullseye despite four prior pushes.
ABX is ABM by another name at a giant reliable sponsor; the keyword score of 60 is flat wrong on this one.
Adobe B2B performance marketing at Specialist level — right seniority, huge sponsor, and the 60 fit score is a scraping artifact.
Radar is fraud/risk for payments — her banking domain is a genuine differentiator here, and Stripe lists remote.
Customer marketing = case studies and customer proof, which she's shipped; Datadog sponsors, but four repeats means apply or drop it.
Remote-US marketing analyst with SQL/attribution is her cleanest lane-2 title — but prev=4 says she keeps skipping it; decide today.
Associate-level GTM ops at Datadog is correctly pitched below manager — good level fit and a real sponsor.
Associate Growth Marketing on paid LinkedIn: right level, and her funnel/attribution metrics work is exactly the evaluation criteria.
Another non-senior Datadog PMM seat; applying to two Datadog PMM reqs is fine and doubles the odds of one recruiter screen.
Stripe GTM planning, US-remote, fintech domain — program-manager framing is a slight stretch from PMM but the content is GTM ops.
Associate Field Marketing is deliberately junior and East-region — closest thing to a Boston-adjacent Datadog entry point.
Promotions analytics is marketing analytics with a different label; SQL + campaign measurement transfer directly.
MongoDB sponsors reliably and lifecycle/PLG growth is a legitimate pivot, but three prior pushes with no action.
B2B marketing in Boston at a NASDAQ company is the best local geography on the board — the repeat count, not the fit, is the problem.
Remote-US Stripe lifecycle growth; solid, but lifecycle/email is the thinnest part of her stack versus ABM and positioning.
Remote-US GTM analytics is a strong lane-2 fit, though Lattice is mid-size and a slower sponsorship bet than the big names.
Boston, right level, but brand marketing pulls away from the B2B GTM narrative she's built.
Boston and Klaviyo sponsors, but 'Product Owner, Sales Systems' is a systems-admin lane that would sidetrack the PMM track.
AWS ABM manager is a true skills match; Arlington VA relocation and three prior passes push it down, not the content.
Remote-US demand gen — her actual title-level work — but Grafana is smaller and the sponsorship path is less proven.
Boston BA role she's seen four times without acting; mid-size company means a real sponsorship question worth asking upfront.
Amazon BA III with an AMZ job number is a PERM/immigration-linked posting — signals sponsorship culture but rarely a live hiring req.
Associate marketing ops is level-perfect, but four repeats and a low ATS score mean it's not converting — last call.
Demand gen at a fintech-adjacent company fits, but a legal-vertical niche plus four prior pushes makes this the one to retire.
